To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in the early 1990s, agricultural production declined in most transition economies, but in some countries production recovered; (ii) the recovery in agricultural production has not been accompanied by a significant increase in agricultural exports, and in some countries agricultural exports have declined; (iii) agricultural prices have increased, but the increases have been insufficient to offset the decline in production; and (iv) agricultural production has declined in the former Soviet Union, and the decline is likely to continue.
